LESSON: PAINTING AND MONTAGE

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade four
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS
Strand: Creating and Executing
Topic 1.3: Painting and Montage
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 15

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Painting and Montage, part of Creating and Executing in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade four CREATIVE ARTS.

Key inquiry question: How do you improvise glue for pasting pictures? 2. Why is colour classification important in painting?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify montage compositions for familiarity,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Painting and Montage in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. classify colours into primary and secondary for painting,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Painting and Montage in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. paint a picture of simple items for colour value application,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Painting and Montage in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. create a montage composition for expression,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Painting and Montage in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. appreciate painting and montage as methods of making pictures.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Painting and Montage in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify montage compositions for familiarity,

   Painting and Montage helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. classify colours into primary and secondary for painting,

   Painting and Montage helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. paint a picture of simple items for colour value application,

   Painting and Montage helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. create a montage composition for expression,

   Painting and Montage helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. appreciate painting and montage as methods of making pictures.

   Painting and Montage helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

F. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1.  observe sample pictures to identify painting and montage composition,  mix primary colours to create secondary colours. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body or use assistive technology.  mix white with a secondary colour to create light tones on a scale strip,  mix black with a secondary colour to create dark tones on a scale strip  paint a picture emphasis colour value,  source picture for relevant pictures and cut out,  arrange and paste cut out pictures to make a montage 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1.  observe sample pictures to identify painting and montage composition,  mix primary colours to create secondary colours. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body or use assistive technology.  mix white with a secondary colour to create light tones on a scale strip,  mix black with a secondary colour to create dark tones on a scale strip  paint a picture emphasis colour value,  source picture for relevant pictures and cut out,  arrange and paste cut out pictures to make a montage 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Painting and Montage together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
 Communication and Collaboration: the learner works with others in groups and speaks clearly about their own and others

work.

 Creativity and Imagination: learner makes thoughtful choices when producing a montage pictorial composition.

Values:
 Respect: Learner accommodates others’ views during critique of their own and others’ original rhythmic compositions.

 Love: Inculcated as the learner take turns to talk about their own and others work.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Social Cohesion: The learner acquires the skill of working with others during creating a montage composition.
